channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Four nonprofits sue OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta and SpaceX to freeze frontier AI development
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Four nonprofits filed suit in San Francisco on November 12, asking a judge to bar the five biggest AI labs from building anything more capable than today’s frontier models — and they built their case from the labs’ own incident reports and warnings.

item.title: Build your first Claude Managed Agent: a hosted agent that codes in its own sandbox
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic's Managed Agents API runs the whole agent loop — harness, sandbox, and session state — on its own servers. This tutorial builds a working coding agent with the Python SDK, verifies every call against SDK 2.8.0, and prices the run to the cent.

item.title: Steam's AI disclosure is backfiring: Big Walk's 0.1% chatbot assist sparked a review backlash
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: House House says large language models touched well under 0.1% of Big Walk's code. That disclosure — and a second from a solo developer this week — has turned Steam's AI transparency rule into a lightning rod.

item.title: Anthropic lets enterprises self-host the full Claude Managed Agents stack — private beta now open
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic opened a private beta on November 12 that lets companies run the entire Claude Managed Agents service inside their own cloud or data center — server, database, workers, credentials and session history included. The model itself stays outside, and a few hosted features do not make the trip.

item.title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, forensic report finds
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A forensic analysis of published model weights finds six recent Chinese models carry numerical patterns matching Nvidia’s export-controlled Blackwell GPUs — the first technical evidence behind years of allegations. The report itself stresses what the fingerprint does not prove.

item.title: Stanford’s Flash ALOHA learns fast, precise robot manipulation from just 50 demos per task
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 74-second clip from Stanford shows a two-armed robot catching a ball, folding shorts, and bussing a table at near-human speed — learned from just 50 demonstrations per task, with the code now open source.

item.title: ElevenLabs bets the company on enterprise agents: 13 products, a meeting app, and a bigger Nvidia deal
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: ElevenLabs used its first New York Summit to pitch itself as enterprise infrastructure: 13 products led by the ElevenAI meeting app, custom models tuned on customer data, and a bigger Nvidia deal — though about half of it is still preview or roadmap.

item.title: Reuters: Jensen Huang had a third affair — and has agreed to testify before Congress
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Hours after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, Reuters reported he had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee — a third woman linked to the scandal. He has also agreed to testify before Congress about the national-security questions around it.

item.title: Adobe opens Photoshop and Premiere to rival AI agents — and turns Firefly into a multi-model creative studio
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: At MAX 2026 in Miami, Adobe said rival AI agents will soon be able to edit native Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects files on your own machine — while Firefly becomes a multi-model studio with its own always-on agents.

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its fast agent model, at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Hours after the name leaked in Google Cloud’s price list, Google confirmed Gemini 4 Hydrogen: a fast, agent-focused model adapted from Carbon, priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens and rolling out globally today.

item.title: Fed’s Bowman warns of a sharp AI-driven market correction as AI debt tops $800 billion
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said on November 10 that AI-related debt is on track to exceed $800 billion this year — and that if AI revenues keep falling short of costs, the result could be a sharp correction in AI share prices, tighter credit, and a slower buildout.

item.title: RUMOR: Unannounced Gemini 4 Hydrogen appears in Google Cloud’s price list at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google hasn’t announced a third Gemini 4 model — but its own billing catalog now lists “Gemini 4 Hydrogen” with full prices, and trackers say the model answers on Vertex AI. Here’s what the listing proves, and what it doesn’t.

item.title: Trump as Morpheus, Jensen Huang as Neo: AI 'Matrix' Parody Goes Viral on Reddit
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 42-second AI Matrix parody casts Donald Trump as Morpheus and Nvidia chief Jensen Huang as Neo, ending with a Xi Jinping jumpscare. Posted to r/ChatGPT overnight, it has 2,200 upvotes and a thread arguing over the lip sync, the tool that made it, and whether the joke flatters its stars.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 hands-on: build a long-horizon coding agent with effort, prompt caching, and fast mode
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic's flagship is 20% cheaper and 30% faster than Fable 5.1 — but the API has four new ways to return a 400. This tutorial builds a working agent loop on the Messages API, verifies every call against SDK 2.8.0, and prices each run to the cent.

item.title: Trellis Data launches Agentaus 1, a 220B-parameter model for sovereign AI
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Canberra-based Trellis Data has launched Agentaus 1, a 220-billion-parameter model it pitches as Australia’s sovereign AI answer — locally hosted, defence-grade encrypted, and timed to Canberra’s new AI safety rules. The benchmark claims, though, are the company’s own word so far.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Nvidia’s board announced on November 12 that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.

item.title: Find, validate, and fix vulnerabilities with OpenAI's Codex Security CLI — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI puts an agentic security reviewer in your terminal: install it, run a full scan–validate–patch loop with no sign-in using mock mode, then wire the same commands into CI with a $5 cost cap.

item.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max preview: a million-token flagship, Token Plan only, gone November 25
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Alibaba opened a two-week preview of Qwen4-Max, the first model of its next-generation Qwen family: a multimodal reasoning model with a million-token context, available only through its Token Plan subscription — and retired when the window closes on November 25. No weights, no benchmarks, no price per token yet.

item.title: Clone any voice on your own machine: hands-on with Zyphra's ZONOS3-Mini
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Zyphra's ZONOS3-Mini clones a voice from a 60-second clip, steers pace, emotion and accent word by word, and runs on an ordinary CPU — no GPU, no account, no fee. Here's the full hands-on: the browser studio, the ggml CLI, cloning, steering, and a local server.

item.title: A local world model you can steer with WASD just landed on Hugging Face — and it runs on an RTX 3060
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: LucidML turns a single image into a playable video you steer in real time — a 630M-parameter world model trained from scratch, with open weights and a live demo that runs on consumer GPUs.

item.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking its flights — the first US carrier to draw the line
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: United rewrote its Contract of Carriage on November 11 to bar AI agents from buying tickets, seats or upgrades — and says it can cancel any reservation an agent touches. Searching is still allowed; checkout is not.

item.title: British AI chip startup Fractile raises $720M at a $7B valuation, with UK state backing
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Fractile, a London- and Bristol-based startup designing chips for AI inference, has raised $720 million at a $7 billion valuation — with the UK government’s Sovereign AI fund and the British Business Bank in the round. The catch: the company has never shipped a chip, and the state won’t say how much of its own money is in the deal.

item.title: Palantir's Alex Karp says he's a lifelong Democrat and the company is 'essentially progressive'
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Days after the Democrats' midterm wins, Palantir CEO Alex Karp told Politico he has 'been a Democrat my whole life,' called the company's products 'essentially progressive,' and opened the door to backing a Democrat in 2028 — a sharp turn for the chief of the Trump administration's closest AI contractor.

item.title: DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2: DNA variant predictions, cell by cell
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how a DNA variant changes gene activity in one specific cell type at a time, recovering nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor. Non-commercial access is open now through the AlphaGenome API.

item.title: Your AI coding agent may have leaked your API keys to GitHub — how to find and purge them
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Apiiro found 2,539 real secrets in public repos after Claude Code's "don't ask again" button saved them verbatim. Audit your own repos with Gitleaks and TruffleHog, purge leaked secrets from git history, and stop it happening again.
